# Dynamics 365 Partner in Dubai for UAE and GCC Enterprises

Choosing a Dynamics 365 partner in Dubai is easier once you know which application you need and how to test the firms on your shortlist. This page gives you both. It sets out a decision rule for Business Central, Finance and Supply Chain Management, Sales, Customer Service and Project Operations. It also gives you a scorecard you can apply to any partner and the decisions behind each phase of a sound implementation. Use it to arrive at partner meetings with clear requirements and sharper questions.

**Quick answer:** A Dynamics 365 partner in Dubai helps UAE businesses choose the right Microsoft Dynamics 365 applications, then implements, integrates and supports them under local tax and reporting rules. To choose one, check that its Microsoft designation can be verified, that its team is based in the UAE, that it has references for your product and industry, and what support it gives after go-live.

[Image: Dynamics 365 partner in Dubai: ERP finance dashboard on a laptop overlooking the Dubai business district]

## What a Dynamics 365 partner in Dubai does

A Dynamics 365 partner in Dubai helps UAE businesses choose the right Microsoft Dynamics 365 applications, then implements, integrates and supports them under local tax and reporting rules. Northwind is a Microsoft partner with an office in Example Free Zone (Example Free Zone), serving enterprises across the UAE and the GCC.

A full-service partner should cover five areas:

1. Licensing and solution advice before you buy licences, so you pay only for the applications your processes need.
2. Implementation and deployment, from configuration through to go-live.
3. Migration and modernisation, including legacy Dynamics AX, NAV and GP.
4. Integration with your banks, e-commerce platforms and any other systems you keep.
5. Ongoing support once the system is live.

Dynamics 365 rarely works alone. Power Platform adds apps and automation, and Microsoft Fabric turns your data into reporting. Copilot for Microsoft 365 and Dynamics 365 Copilot bring AI into daily work, all running on Microsoft cloud services.

### What is the difference between a Dynamics 365 partner and a CRM partner?

A CRM-only partner works on Sales and Customer Service. A Dynamics 365 partner also covers ERP: finance, supply chain and operations. With one partner across both, your front and back office share a single data model. A customer order, its invoice and its stock movement sit in the same system instead of being reconciled across separate ones.

The trade-off is simple. If your only problem is the sales pipeline, a CRM specialist may be enough. If finance and customer data must match, look for a partner that covers both.

## Which Dynamics 365 application fits your business?

Business Central suits single companies and growing groups with standard finance, sales and inventory needs. Finance and Supply Chain Management suits multi-entity groups with complex finance, supply chain or cross-border operations. Sales and Customer Service fit customer-facing teams, and Project Operations fits firms that sell and deliver projects. Confirm the choice with a gap-fit analysis.

Three questions decide it:

- How many legal entities and countries will run on the system.
- How complex your finance and supply chain processes are.
- How fast you expect to add companies, markets or product lines.

Choose Business Central if you run one company or a small group with standard processes. Choose Finance and Supply Chain Management, often called Finance & Operations, if you run several entities, manufacture, hold stock across countries or consolidate in more than one currency.

[Image: Decision tree for choosing between Business Central, Finance and Supply Chain Management, Dynamics 365 Sales and Project Operations]

| Application | Best suited to | What it covers | Signs you need it |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Dynamics 365 Business Central in the UAE](https://www.northwind.example/dynamics-365-business-central-uae) | Single companies and smaller groups with standard processes | Finance, sales, purchasing and inventory in one ERP | Spreadsheets fill the gaps between accounting and stock, and entry-level accounting software no longer copes |
| [Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations](https://www.northwind.example/dynamics-365-finance-and-operations-uae) | Multi-entity groups, manufacturers and distributors | Multi-entity finance, consolidation, supply chain, warehousing and manufacturing | Intercompany entries are made by hand, you trade in several countries, or warehouses and production are complex |
| [Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service](https://www.northwind.example/dynamics-365-crm-uae) | Sales and service teams | Leads, opportunities, quotes, cases and service queues | The pipeline lives in inboxes and nobody has one view of customer history |
| Project Operations | Consulting, engineering and professional services firms | Quotes, resources, time and billing, running on Dataverse | Utilisation and project margin are only known after the project ends |

### Business Central or Finance & Operations?

The line is less about company size than about structure. If you expect to stay within one or two entities and standard processes, Business Central keeps licences and configuration lighter. If you already run several legal entities, or plan acquisitions and new countries, Finance & Operations supports multi-entity go-live, intercompany and consolidation without workarounds.

Avoid buying the smaller product for a group structure you will soon reach. Moving later means a second implementation project.

### When do Sales, Customer Service or Project Operations come first?

Start with CRM when revenue leaks through the pipeline or the service backlog, and your finance system works well enough. Start with Project Operations when projects are your product.

ERP and CRM apps can be combined on the same platform. The order and scope should come out of a gap-fit analysis of your processes, not a licence price list.

## How do you choose a Dynamics 365 partner in the UAE?

Check the partner's Microsoft designation on Microsoft's own listing, confirm the delivery team is based in the UAE, and ask for references for your product and industry. Then check its Arabic and tax localisation, how it connects Dynamics 365 to your accredited e-invoicing provider, and what support and handover it gives after go-live.

[Image: Scorecard for comparing Dynamics 365 partners in the UAE across six criteria including localisation and support]

### A scorecard for your shortlist

Score every partner on the same criteria. Check each claim yourself rather than accepting a logo on a slide.

- Microsoft designation. How to check it: search for the partner on Microsoft's own partner directory and confirm the designation matches the one claimed.
- UAE-based delivery team. How to check it: ask for the names and locations of the consultants on your project, and who will be on site.
- Localisation. How to check it: ask for a demo of Arabic and English users and UAE VAT and Corporate Tax set-up, and confirm current VAT rules on [tax.gov.ae](https://tax.gov.ae), where the regulatory requirements for businesses across the UAE are published.
- References. How to check it: speak to clients on the same product and in a similar industry.
- Integration depth. How to check it: ask how the partner has connected Dynamics 365 to banks, e-commerce platforms and legacy systems, and who maintains each connection.
- Support and handover. How to check it: read the support terms before you sign, not after go-live.

### What to ask about e-invoicing and support

Under [Ministerial Decision No. 66 of 2026](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Ministerial-Resolution-No.-66-of-2026-Amending-Certain-Provisions-of-Ministerial-Resolution-No.-244-of-2025-Regarding-the-Implementation-of-the-Electronic-Invoicing-System-En-20260514.pdf), a business with revenue equal to or exceeding AED 50,000,000 must appoint an Accredited Service Provider by 30 October 2026 and implement the Electronic Invoicing System by 1 January 2027. Under [Ministerial Decision No. 244 of 2025](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Ministerial-Decision-No.-244-of-2025-on-the-Implementation-of-the-Electronic-Invoicing-System.pdf), businesses below AED 50,000,000 must appoint one by 31 March 2027 and implement by 1 July 2027. Government entities must appoint one by 31 March 2027 and implement by 1 October 2027.

For your ERP decision, ask each partner how its Dynamics 365 design connects to your Ministry of Finance accredited service provider. Ask who builds and owns that integration, and who fixes it when an invoice is rejected. Our guide on [what to look for in Peppol e-invoicing software](https://www.northwind.example/insights/top-peppol-e-invoicing-software-features-every-uae-cfo-must-look-for) covers the provider side.

Then put these questions to every shortlisted firm:

1. Who exactly does the work, and are they employees or subcontractors?
2. What is in scope, and what is written down as out of scope?
3. How are change requests priced and approved?
4. What is the data migration plan, and who cleans the data?
5. Who supports the system after go-live?

### What support should you expect after go-live?

Expect named support contacts and response targets written into the contract. You should also get a defined hypercare period, a plan for Microsoft release waves and updates, and documentation plus admin training at handover. Without these, your team depends on the partner for every small change, and knowledge leaves when a consultant does.

## What drives the cost and timeline of a Dynamics 365 implementation?

Cost and duration depend on the application, number of users and legal entities, how much is customised rather than standard, the number of integrations, data migration volume and how quickly the business makes decisions. Ask every vendor for a phased, itemised proposal against the same requirements, with dated phase gates and written change control.

### How much does a Dynamics 365 implementation cost in the UAE?

No reliable figure exists without your requirements. Licence subscriptions, implementation services and ongoing support are separate cost lines, so compare each one separately. A low services quote with heavy customisation, or one that leaves data migration out of scope, can cost more by the end. Ask each vendor to price the same requirements document.

### How long does a Dynamics 365 rollout take?

Duration follows the same drivers, plus two that sit with you: how quickly your team makes decisions and how ready your data is. A project that waits for process sign-off loses that time at every gate. Ask for a plan with dated phase gates and named decision owners on your side.

### Phases and the decisions each one needs

1. Discovery and requirements. Decision: who signs off the process scope for finance, operations and sales.
2. Gap-fit analysis. Decision: for each gap, whether to use a standard feature, change the process or customise.
3. Build and configuration. Decision: approval of the solution design, and the point at which scope is frozen.
4. Testing with real users. Decision: who tests, with which real transactions, and what counts as a pass.
5. Data migration. Decision: how much history to bring across and which records to archive instead.
6. Go-live. Decision: the cut-over approach and the go or no-go criteria.
7. Hypercare. Decision: when support moves from the project team to everyday support.

### A budget-risk checklist

- Freeze scope before build starts. Late changes cost the most because they touch work already done.
- Prefer standard features to custom code, which has to be retested with every Microsoft update.
- Clean data early. Otherwise, bad master data surfaces during migration, when fixing it disrupts the plan.
- Budget for change management and training, not only software and configuration.
- Agree change control in the contract, with a written process for pricing and approving changes.
- Treat legacy AX, NAV or GP migration as its own workstream. If you are [upgrading from Dynamics AX](https://www.northwind.example/dynamics-ax-to-d365-upgrade-uae), map existing customisations first, because some may be replaced by standard features.

## Who Northwind works with and how engagements run

We work with enterprises across the UAE and the GCC in banking and financial services, public sector, education and training, tourism and hospitality, trading and manufacturing, retail, professional services and non-profit.

Our engagements start with Assess & Envision, which covers business discovery, requirements, gap-fit analysis and an ROI assessment. Build & Implement delivers the solution on Dynamics 365 business applications, Microsoft Fabric and Power Platform. Run & Optimise, Global Rollouts, Managed Services and AI & Automation cover what comes next, depending on your needs.

We work across Dynamics 365 Finance, Supply Chain Management, Sales, Customer Service, Field Service, Project Operations, Human Resources, Commerce and Business Central. We also deliver cloud services and data, plus AI capabilities including Copilot Studio, Azure OpenAI Service and AI Builder.

We have 20+ years of industry experience and provide 24/7 support. For the period after go-live, see our [Dynamics 365 managed services](https://www.northwind.example/dynamics-365-managed-services-uae).

If you are comparing options for a Dynamics 365 partner in Dubai, book a consultation with Northwind to talk through your Dynamics 365 plans, product choice or migration.
